customerJourneyStories.name: Switching from an outdated till to Vendit
customerJourneyStories.summary: An owner whose old till cannot keep up with a webshop moves to Vendit with hardware, migration and training included.

stages.narrative: The old till vendor stops updates and the webshop stock no longer matches the shop; a customer is told "sold out" while the bike stands in the back room.
A fellow member of the branch association (for jewellers, the FGZ partnership) and a supplier mention Vendit; the owner finds branch pages and success stories online.
An online demo shows supplier links and the dashboard; the owner compares the fixed monthly fee and included migration with Lightspeed and a branch specialist and checks references.
Vendit migrates articles and customers, installs the hardware and trains staff; the first Saturday runs on Vendit with support on standby.
Daily dashboard checks become routine; the owner adds the webshop module and later the marketplace module.
Saved time on supplier data and stock and the cost of switching again keep the owner on Vendit; they recommend it in the branch network.

customerJourneyStories.name: Replacing a system that could not keep up with growth
customerJourneyStories.summary: A growing chain replaces a slow, fragmented system with Vendit Enterprise.

stages.narrative: Opening a third branch shows that prices differ per store and stock transfers are tracked in spreadsheets.
The manager hears of Vendit through a supplier and Katapull customer stories, and shortlists it next to Lightspeed and a full ERP such as Logic4.
Evaluation focuses on branch control, unlimited users, B2B invoicing and data migration; references from comparable chains are called.
One branch goes live first while the others stay on the old system for a few weeks; central price publication is tested on a promotion.
All branches run on Vendit; the dashboard by branch becomes the weekly management meeting agenda.
The chain stays because adding branches is routine; when online volume grows it evaluates Logic4 within the same group rather than a new vendor.

customerJourneyStories.name: Rolling out Vendit to all formula members
customerJourneyStories.summary: An RSO standardises its members on Vendit to regain central control, as the KW Groep did for Blokker entrepreneurs.

stages.narrative: A formula change (new ownership, new entrepreneurs) leaves members on different systems and campaigns cannot be pushed centrally.
The RSO knows Vendit from other franchise organisations and from its filiaal solution for RSOs.
Evaluation covers central publication, member data sharing, purchase formulas and a group price; Vendit demonstrates with formula data.
A pilot group of stores goes live with "a flying start"; first central campaign is executed through Vendit.
All members run on Vendit; head office plans campaigns knowing they will be executed everywhere.
The formula renews because switching all members again is costly and the shared data has become the basis for formula management.

customerJourneyStories.name: Getting comfortable with the new till
customerJourneyStories.summary: A sales associate learns Vendit when the store switches systems.

stages.narrative: The owner announces a new till; the associate worries about Saturday queues.
They first see Vendit in the demo the owner arranged and in training material.
During training they try returns, trade-ins and gift cards and judge how many clicks a sale takes.
First Saturday on Vendit with support reachable; a few lookups take longer than before.
After a few weeks checkout is routine and they use stock lookup across branches to save sales.
They prefer staying on Vendit because it is familiar; they become the go-to colleague for new staff.

customerJourneyStories.name: From paper tickets to the digital workshop board
customerJourneyStories.summary: A technician adopts Vendit repair management.

stages.narrative: Spring rush: paper tickets get lost and two customers come back for bikes that were not started.
The owner shows the Vendit workshop functions highlighted for the two-wheeler trade.
The technician checks that frame numbers, parts and labour fit on one order and that customers get messages.
For two weeks new repairs go into Vendit while old tickets are finished on paper.
The board is the morning routine; ready messages replace phone calls.
Going back to paper is unthinkable; the technician asks for photo attachments as next improvement.

customerJourneyStories.name: Adding marketplaces without adding workload
customerJourneyStories.summary: A coordinator adopts the Vendit marketplace module with EffectConnect.

stages.narrative: Management wants to sell on bol, but uploading listings by hand would take days and stock would not stay in sync.
The coordinator reads Vendit's marketplace module page and a success story of a retailer growing with EffectConnect.
They check which marketplaces are supported, the per-5,000-article scaling and how orders and labels flow back.
A first product group goes live on bol; orders appear in Vendit and labels print via DeliveryMatch.
More groups and Amazon follow; checking listing errors becomes a daily routine.
The coordinator stays because marketplace, shop and webshop share one article master.

customerJourneyStories.name: Becoming a regular of a local specialist
customerJourneyStories.summary: A shopper experiences a Vendit-run store across channels (the shopper never sees Vendit by name).

stages.narrative: The shopper needs a specific item and does not want a wasted trip.
They find the store's webshop through search or a marketplace listing.
They compare price and availability with large online players and choose the store because stock is shown and advice is local.
They reserve or buy online and pick up, or buy in store; a customer card is offered at checkout.
Saving points, repair updates and receipts by e-mail make them return.
They stay loyal to the store and buy gift cards for others.

customerJourneyStories.name: Connecting to Vendit retailers
customerJourneyStories.summary: A wholesaler sets up an electronic connection with Vendit to serve its dealer network.

stages.narrative: Dealers keep phoning in orders and using old prices.
Several dealers say they run Vendit and ask for a connection; Vendit states it is linked with all national bike suppliers.
The supplier evaluates file formats and EDI through Transus versus a direct connection.
A pilot with a few dealers exchanges article files and orders.
All Vendit dealers order electronically; frame numbers arrive with delivery data.
The connection stays because it serves the whole dealer base.
